departments.name: Game Engine Architecture
departments.mission: Choose and shape the runtime: engine, rendering path, game loop, scene model, entity architecture, memory strategy and platform compatibility.

deliverables.name: Engine Decision Record
acceptance: Each candidate engine scored against the GDD's hard requirements
Decision recorded as an ADR with alternatives and rejected reasons
Licensing, team skill and platform support addressed
Migration cost stated if the decision is later reversed

deliverables.name: Runtime Architecture
acceptance: Game loop, update order and frame budget documented
Scene graph or ECS model and its ownership rules described
Memory budgets per subsystem and allocation policy stated
Every module has an owning department

deliverables.name: Platform and Build Matrix
acceptance: Every supported platform listed with target resolution and quality tier
Build and export commands recorded and runnable
Input devices and storefront constraints listed per platform

inputs: hardware classes from the performance profiles
gates: A code change that breaks the existing typecheck or build is rejected
Architecture decisions without an ADR are rejected

departments.name: Gameplay Programming
departments.mission: Implement the game the player touches: controllers, movement, combat, interaction, inventory, abilities and progression.
capabilities: gameplay state machines and save hooks

deliverables.name: Controller and Input Spec
acceptance: Input map for every declared device
Movement model with speeds, acceleration and camera rules
Remapping, dead zones and accessibility input options covered

deliverables.name: Playable Prototype
acceptance: The core loop is playable end to end in a real build
Build command and URL or artefact path recorded in the deliverable
Known gaps listed explicitly rather than hidden

deliverables.name: Gameplay Systems
acceptance: Every GDD mechanic implemented with its failure and feedback states
Telemetry hooks emitted for every tuned value
No gameplay value hard-coded outside the tuning table

deliverables.name: Gameplay Test Evidence
acceptance: Automated checks cover movement, interaction and progression paths
Manual playthrough evidence attached for the core loop
Any known defect linked to a bug report

gates: A gameplay mechanic with no failure state or no feedback is rejected
Unhandled input device or missing remap path is rejected

departments.name: Physics Engineering
departments.mission: Make the world solid and believable: collision, rigid bodies, projectiles, destruction, vehicles and terrain interaction.

deliverables.name: Physics Specification
acceptance: Fixed timestep, substeps and interpolation policy stated
Collision layers and their interactions tabulated
Determinism requirements stated for multiplayer or replay use

deliverables.name: Collision and Body Setup
acceptance: Every collidable object has an appropriate collider and layer
Character controller handles slopes, steps and edges without sticking
Projectiles and destructibles behave to the GDD numbers

deliverables.name: Physics Validation
acceptance: No tunnelling through walls at maximum speed
Object counts at peak measured against the physics budget
Known edge cases documented with reproduction steps

gates: Tunnelling or stuck-geometry defects are release blockers
Physics costs over budget without a listed fix are rejected

departments.name: AI Engineering
departments.mission: Give the world intelligence: enemies, allies, civilians, wildlife and strategic actors that make readable, fair decisions.

deliverables.name: AI Design
acceptance: Every AI archetype listed with role, senses and decision model
Fairness rules stated: reaction time, accuracy and information limits
Navigation and spawn constraints stated per archetype

deliverables.name: Behaviour and Navigation Systems
acceptance: Every archetype implemented and observable in a build
Pathfinding handles the whole playable space without getting stuck
AI update cost measured per frame against its budget

deliverables.name: AI Validation
acceptance: No archetype can be farmed with a single degenerate strategy
Stuck, idle or unreachable agents counted at zero in a soak run
Reaction time measured and within the fairness rule

inputs: world layout and navmesh from D08
gates: An AI archetype without a fairness rule is rejected
Unbounded per-frame AI cost is rejected

departments.name: Multiplayer Engineering
departments.mission: Make networked play work: authority, replication, matchmaking, latency handling and anti-cheat structure.

deliverables.name: Netcode Architecture
acceptance: Authority model stated per system (server, client, hybrid)
Tick rate, snapshot rate and bandwidth budget in numbers
Trust boundary drawn and every client-supplied value validated server-side

deliverables.name: Replication and Session Layer
acceptance: Players join, play and leave a session without desync
Reconnect restores authoritative state
Bandwidth measured in a full session against the budget

deliverables.name: Network Validation
acceptance: Two-client test evidence attached including unauthorised actions rejected
Simulated latency and packet loss behaviour documented
No client-authoritative value can grant an unfair advantage

gates: A client-authoritative gameplay value is a release blocker
Netcode without measured bandwidth is rejected

departments.name: Backend and Data Engineering
departments.mission: Keep player state safe and useful: save systems, profiles, cloud persistence, accounts, leaderboards, telemetry and analytics.
capabilities: save and load formats with migrations
API design between client and service

deliverables.name: Data Model and API Contract
acceptance: Every persisted entity and field typed and versioned
Save migration path from every shipped version stated
API endpoints or bindings listed with their authorisation rules

deliverables.name: Persistence Layer
acceptance: Save, load and migration proven by an automated round-trip test
Corrupt or partial saves recovered or rejected without data loss
Every write validated server-side where a server exists

deliverables.name: Save Integrity and Analytics Review
acceptance: Save tampering detected and handled
Analytics events verified as delivered and non-blocking
Storage growth projected against the retention policy

gates: A save format without a migration path is rejected
Client-trusted economy or progression writes are a release blocker
